ShortDescription.Value: Ported using Claude AI (Anthropic). Place a chain of points and get live elevation, distance, slope, and direction readouts between them - including bridges, tunnels, and buried pipes.

Publish.LongDescription:
Ported from the original CS1 mod using Claude AI (Anthropic).
Original CS1 mod can be found here: [https://github.com/keallu/CSL-MeasureIt](https://github.com/keallu/CSL-MeasureIt)
Measure It! for CS2 lets you place a chain of points anywhere in your city and get instant elevation, distance, slope, and direction readouts between them - a port of the classic Measure It! mod, rebuilt for Cities: Skylines II.
FEATURES:
Place multiple measurement points ; each segment gets its own row in the mod window, plus running totals for the whole chain.
Choose your units: Meters, Kilometers, Feet, or Miles for distance; Percentage or Degrees for slope; Degrees or Cardinal (N/NE/E/...) for direction.
Draggable mod window that remembers its position between uses.
Change color of points and lines in mods options menu (Color choices include Yellow, Magenta, Red, Green, Cyan, White and Orange.).
Numbered point markers on the map that match the segment table in the mods window.
Works on elevated bridges and inside tunnels, not just flat ground.
Snap to nodes: clicks snap to actual road, pipe, track, and subway nodes - measure precisely to/through buried pipes and underground lines, not just visible surfaces (Snap to nodes feature can be toggled on andoff by clicking on the checkmark box in the mod's window.).
Connecting lines follow the real network route between two snapped points (tracing the actual curve of the road, pipe, or subway line) instead of just cutting a straight line between them.
Rebindable keyboard shortcuts.
Toolbar icon is located in the game's Universal Mod Menu.
HOW TO USE:
1. Click the ruler icon in the Universal Mod Menu, or press Ctrl+M, to activate the tool.
2. Left-click on the map to place a point. Keep clicking to build a chain.
3. Right-click (or Ctrl+X) to undo the last point.
4. Adjust point color, and keybinds from Options -> Measure It! for CS2.
5. Adjust units, snap-to-nodes and measurements from the mod window.
FEEDBACK AND BUG REPORTS:
Please open an issue on the GitHub repository linked below.
[Measure It! for CS2 on GitHub](https://github.com/Route66Fan/MeasureItCS2)

ChangeLog.Value: Added support for the Cities: Skylines II editor (toggle the tool with Ctrl+M). Point numbers now follow the game's active camera.
